chunks: I asked him about the day in which there is a doubt about whether it is from the month of Ramadan — one does not know whether it is from Sha'ban or from Ramadan — and one fasted it, and it turned out to be from the month of Ramadan. He said: It is a day of success granted to him, and there is no make-up obligation upon him.

key_terms.قَضَاء: Make-up obligation — the requirement to fast an additional day to compensate for a missed or invalid fast
key_terms.وُفِّقَ لَهُ: He was granted tawfiq (divine enabling/success) — the fast counted because God guided him to it
key_terms.يَوْمُ الشَّكِّ: The doubtful day — the last day of Sha'ban when the beginning of Ramadan is uncertain due to unclear moon sighting

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one fasts the doubtful day and it turns out to be Ramadan?
ai.summary: Sama'ah asked the Imam about the ruling on the 'doubtful day' (yawm al-shakk) — the last day of Sha'ban when it is unclear whether Ramadan has begun. If a person fasts this day with uncertainty and it turns out to be the first day of Ramadan, the Imam rules that no make-up fast (qada') is required. The Imam characterizes this as a day of divine tawfiq (success/enabling grace), meaning God facilitated the person's observance of the obligatory fast even amid uncertainty.
word_analysis: and it turned out to be
